017package org.apache.juneau.examples.mcp.secured;
018
019import java.net.*;
020
021import org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.*;
022import org.apache.juneau.microservice.*;
023import org.apache.juneau.microservice.jetty.*;
024import org.eclipse.jetty.ee11.servlet.*;
025import org.eclipse.jetty.server.*;
026
027import jakarta.servlet.*;
028
029/**
030 * Boots {@link SecuredExampleMcpServer} on an embedded Jetty server, alongside an in-process
031 * {@link OfflineAuthorizationServer} that stands in for a real OAuth 2.1 authorization server.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * Mirrors {@link org.apache.juneau.examples.mcp.ExampleServer} (read that class first &mdash; this one only
035 * documents what is different). Run {@link #main(String[]) main} to start both servers on fixed ports and
036 * print everything a {@link SecuredExampleClient} run needs to copy: the endpoint, the offline authorization
037 * server's token endpoint, and the randomly-generated demo client id/secret. The in-process end-to-end test
038 * uses {@link #start(int) start(0)} to boot on an OS-assigned ephemeral port instead.
039 *
040 * <p>
041 * <b>The resource URL is resolved before the secured servlet is even constructed.</b> {@link SecuredExampleMcpServer}
042 * needs its own address up front (see its class javadoc), which is awkward on an OS-assigned ephemeral port
043 * because normally nothing knows that port until Jetty finishes starting. The fix: {@link ServerConnector#open()}
044 * can be, and by Jetty's own convention normally is (see {@code Server.doStart()}'s "open network connector to
045 * ensure ports are available" step), called to bind the listening socket BEFORE the rest of the server starts.
046 * Calling it ourselves, one step earlier than usual, lets us read {@link ServerConnector#getLocalPort()}
047 * immediately &mdash; before building {@link SecuredExampleMcpServer} or starting the {@link Microservice} at
048 * all. Jetty's own {@code Server.start()} then finds the connector already open and skips rebinding it.
049 */
050@SuppressWarnings({
051   "java:S106" // Example walkthrough intentionally prints to stdout; console output is the demo's deliverable.
052})
053public final class SecuredExampleServer implements AutoCloseable {
054
055   /** Default listen port used by {@link #main(String[])} when none is supplied. */
056   public static final int DEFAULT_PORT = 5001;
057
058   private final Microservice microservice;
059   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // closed in close(); this field's lifecycle is fully managed by this class.
060   private final OfflineAuthorizationServer authServer;
061   private final URI rootUrl;
062
063   private SecuredExampleServer(Microservice microservice, OfflineAuthorizationServer authServer, URI rootUrl) {
064      this.microservice = microservice;
065      this.authServer = authServer;
066      this.rootUrl = rootUrl;
067   }
068
069   /**
070    * Starts the secured example MCP server and its offline authorization server.
071    *
072    * @param port The TCP port the MCP server listens on, or {@code 0} to let the OS assign an ephemeral port.
073    *    (The offline authorization server always uses its own separate OS-assigned ephemeral port.)
074    * @return A running server handle. Close it (or call {@link #close()}) to stop both servers.
075    * @throws Exception If either server fails to start.
076    */
077   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // The bean store is handed to (and closed by) the Microservice lifecycle.
078   public static SecuredExampleServer start(int port) throws Exception {
079      var authServer = OfflineAuthorizationServer.start();
080      // M9: hoisted above the try so a failure AFTER connector.open() (which has already bound a real OS
081      // socket) can still close it in the catch below - Server.stop() alone will not close a connector that
082      // was opened but never handed to a started Server.
083      ServerConnector connector = null;
084      try {
085         var jetty = new Server();
086         connector = new ServerConnector(jetty);
087         connector.setPort(port);
088         jetty.addConnector(connector);
089         // Bind the (possibly ephemeral) listen socket now, before the servlet context (and therefore
090         // SecuredExampleMcpServer's RestContext) is built, so the resource URL below is real and final
091         // by the time anything asks the servlet for it. See the class javadoc for why that ordering
092         // matters here specifically.
093         connector.open();
094         var rootUrl = URI.create("http://localhost:" + connector.getLocalPort() + "/");
095
096         var handler = new ServletContextHandler();
097         handler.setContextPath("/");
098         jetty.setAttribute("ServletContextHandler", handler);
099         jetty.setHandler(handler);
100
101         var securedServlet = new SecuredExampleMcpServer(authServer, rootUrl);
102
103         var beanStore = new BasicBeanStore();
104         beanStore.addBean(Server.class, jetty);
105         beanStore.addBean(Servlet.class, securedServlet);
106
107         var microservice = Microservice.create()
108            .beanStore(beanStore)
109            .configurations(JettyConfiguration.class)
110            .consoleEnabled(false)
111            .build();
112         microservice.start();
113
114         return new SecuredExampleServer(microservice, authServer, rootUrl);
115      } catch (Exception e) {
116         if (connector != null)
117            connector.close();
118         authServer.close();
119         throw e;
120      }
121   }
122
123   /**
124    * Returns the root URL the secured MCP server is listening on (e.g. {@code http://localhost:5001/}).
125    *
126    * @return The root URL. Never <jk>null</jk>.
127    */
128   public URI getRootUrl() {
129      return rootUrl;
130   }
131
132   /**
133    * Returns the offline authorization server backing this instance, so a caller (e.g. the end-to-end test,
134    * or {@link #main(String[])} printing a startup banner) can read its token endpoint and demo credentials.
135    *
136    * @return The offline authorization server. Never <jk>null</jk>.
137    */
138   public OfflineAuthorizationServer getAuthServer() {
139      return authServer;
140   }
141
142   @Override
143   public void close() throws Exception {
144      try {
145         microservice.stop();
146      } finally {
147         authServer.close();
148      }
149   }
150
151   /**
152    * Runs both servers until the process is killed, printing everything {@link SecuredExampleClient} needs.
153    *
154    * <p>
155    * M10: the token endpoint is no longer printed here &mdash; {@link SecuredExampleClient} now discovers it
156    * itself via RFC 9728 PRM + RFC 8414 discovery, exactly as a real client would, so only the endpoint and
157    * demo client credentials need to be copied.
158    *
159    * @param args Optional single argument: the port the MCP server listens on (defaults to {@link #DEFAULT_PORT}).
160    * @throws Exception If either server fails to start.
161    */
162   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // example server (and its auth server) run for the JVM lifetime; closed on process exit.
163   public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
164      var port = args.length > 0 ? Integer.parseInt(args[0]) : DEFAULT_PORT;
165      var server = start(port);
166      var auth = server.getAuthServer();
167      System.out.println("Juneau SECURED MCP example server is listening at " + server.getRootUrl());
168      System.out.println("Demo client id:     " + auth.clientId());
169      System.out.println("Demo client secret: " + auth.clientSecret());
170      System.out.println();
171      System.out.println("Drive it with:  SecuredExampleClient " + server.getRootUrl() + " "
172         + auth.clientId() + " " + auth.clientSecret());
173      System.out.println("Press Ctrl-C to stop.");
174      Thread.currentThread().join();
175   }
176}
